content.text: The component balance follows from conservation of atomic identity in a nonreactive separator. Each stream may carry multiple constituents and a process can preferentially enrich one component while discarding another. Overall total-mass conservation can pass even when the desired component's recovery is poor, so species-resolved measurements matter. A thermodynamic separation limit can constrain the minimum work, but real energy demand also depends on transport, irreversibilities and equipment details. No separation technology can be selected safely from a recovery percentage alone.
